cards.title_en: Minimum wage is a legal right
cards.text_en: No employer can pay you less than the minimum wage notified by the government. This applies to daily wage workers as well as monthly workers. If you are paid less, you can complain to the labour authority.

cards.title_en: When your wages must be paid
cards.text_en: Daily wages are paid at the end of the shift. Weekly wages are paid on the last working day before the weekly holiday. Monthly wages are paid before the seventh day of the next month.

cards.title_en: Claiming unpaid wages within three years
cards.text_en: If your employer or contractor has not paid your wages, you can file a claim application with the authority within three years from the date the claim arose. A later claim may be accepted if there is a good reason for the delay.

An employer can make only deductions allowed by law, such as fines for specified misconduct or advances already given. Total deductions are limited to a share of your wages. Cutting your pay without a lawful reason is not allowed.

cards.title_en: No pay discrimination between women and men
cards.text_en: An employer cannot pay a woman less than a man for the same work or work of a similar nature. Equal pay applies to wages, and hiring rules also cannot discriminate on the basis of gender.
If you work more than the normal hours in a day or week, you are entitled to overtime pay at a higher rate, at least twice your normal rate of wages. Ask for a record of the extra hours you worked.

cards.title_en: Minimum wage covers daily wagers and unorganised workers
cards.text_en: The minimum wage rule applies to every worker in the organised and the unorganised sector. Daily wagers, casual labourers and workers hired through a contractor are all covered.

Unorganised workers can register on the e-Shram portal or at a common service centre. Registration is free and you should not pay anyone. Registered workers get a universal account number card and can access welfare schemes.

Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-dhan is a pension scheme for unorganised workers aged 18 to 40 earning up to 15,000 rupees a month. It gives an assured pension of 3,000 rupees a month at age 60. You contribute monthly and the government adds an equal amount.
Workers registered on e-Shram get accident insurance cover of 2 lakh rupees under the PMSBY scheme, for accidental death or permanent disability. You do not pay extra for this cover through e-Shram.

The Code on Social Security provides social security to all unorganised workers, including gig, platform and domestic workers. Benefits include life and disability cover, health and maternity benefit, and old age protection under schemes notified by the government.

cards.title_en: Construction workers: BOCW registration and benefits
cards.text_en: Building and construction workers can register with the state construction workers welfare board. Registered workers can get benefits such as accident help, education aid for children and medical help. Ask the welfare board office for the current list of benefits.

A woman who has worked for the required number of days before delivery is entitled to paid maternity leave and cannot be dismissed because she is pregnant. Coverage for unorganised workers is limited, so ask about the schemes you may qualify for.

cards.title_en: Sexual harassment at work: how to complain
cards.text_en: Sexual harassment at the workplace is against the law. You can complain in writing to the Internal Committee of the workplace, or to the Local Committee of your district if there is no such committee. The complaint has a time limit, so act soon and keep a record of what happened.

The number 14434 is the helpdesk for the e-Shram portal. It can help with registering and using e-Shram and it works in Hindi and several other languages. It does not handle wage claims or workplace complaints.

This assistant gives general information, not legal advice. It cannot file cases, judge your specific dispute or replace a lawyer or a labour officer. For a specific dispute, meet the labour office or a legal aid centre.

cards.title_en: Domestic workers: no separate central law yet
cards.text_en: There is no dedicated central law for domestic workers. They are covered through the general labour codes and some state policies. Domestic work is often paid a fixed monthly amount, so ask your state labour department about local rules.
Domestic workers are included among the unorganised workers who are covered by the Code on Social Security. They can register on e-Shram and apply for the welfare schemes they qualify for.
